The knit collar rises above the jacket's turned collar, and its narrow cuffs emerge beyond the tweed sleeves. Each forearm leads visibly from its own sleeve to its hand. The gathered corner now hangs as a compact vertical tail beneath the ring, while the free upper canvas still bows in the wind. Its painted blue arch is kinked by the pulled fold, making the change in tension visible. Her gaze rests on the attachment, her lips gently parted as the next knot waits to be made. A chalk stage mark and two folded rehearsal chairs situate this brief repair within the rehearsal space. Place the moving canvas toward the right edge and leave breathing space around the attachment. Cool late-afternoon skylight reveals the tweed and wool surfaces; a warm rehearsal lamp by the open theatre door gives a small amber edge to her cheek and knit collar. Keep natural skin texture, believable fabric weight and moderate depth of field, with the subject and contact plane crisp and the distant roof parapet softly receding.
